content: Have the courage to follow your heart and intuition.
author: Steve Jobs
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

Across his life and work, Steve Jobs saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?

practicalInsight: Create something today without editing yourself to suit outside expectations. Let it be raw, honest, and uniquely yours.
originalQuote: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life. Don't be trapped by dogma — which is living with the results of other people's thinking. Don't let the noise of others' opinions drown out your own inner voice. And most importantly, have the courage to follow your heart and intuition. They somehow already know what you truly want to become. Everything else is secondary.
